lots.guide_summary: All sold, all Gowans hammer prices in AUD (rate 1.0), no unsold or asking evidence. The four closest plain or near-plain sterling bangles of 35 to 42g made $50 to $90 hammer between Nov 2025 and Sep 2026 ($90 and $80 for the two plain 35g bands). Heavier or decorative bangles reached $100 to $160. Melt (floor, not a sale): 34.6g x 0.925 = 32.0g fine = 1.029 oz t x A$86.28 (silver US$59.98/oz gold-api.com x 1.4386 AUD/USD frankfurter.app, 7 Oct 2026) = about A$89, if the weight is right. Gowans plain bangles have recently sold at or below melt, so scrap buyers set the market here.
lots.working: Keep: lowest surviving same-or-close SOLD in the last 24 months = $50 hammer (lot 376804, 39.1g, Nov 2025) / 1.198 = 41.7, round down = $40 hammer ($47.92 all-in). The two plain 35g bands ($80, $90) would give $65, but $40 stays inside all four close sales. Flip: likely resale about $96 (what Gowans buyers paid all-in for the plain 35.8g band, $80 x 1.198), sold on eBay at about 13% fees and $10 tracked postage: 96 x 0.87 - 10 = 73.5; 73.5 / 2.396 = 30.7, round down = $30 hammer. Selling as scrap at roughly 80% of the A$89 melt (about $71, no fees) gives 71 / 2.396 = 29.6, so about the same. Inbound freight $0 (pickup Moonah).
lots.confidence_reason: 925 stamp read in photo 3, and four close Gowans SOLD results (two of them plain 35g bands) checked in the API JSON with photos viewed. Weight is the one thing not verified.
lots.dropped_entries: Dropped the $210 hammer lot 391766 (STERLING SILVER BANGLE - BIRMINGHAM - 35.8GM, listed 2026-02-23): its photo shows a wide hinged bangle with applied floral decoration and a safety chain, a decorative English piece, not a plain band. All other researcher prices, dates and titles matched the API exactly. Re-filed lots 393245 and 417639 as same_item yes, and 376804 and 435372 as close (patterned or cuff, heavier).
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 3: '925' punched clearly on the inner face. Photos 1-2: plain flat polished band about 8 to 10mm wide, box-tongue hinge clasp with the catch tongue intact, no maker's mark, no safety chain. Fine all-over surface scratching, small dark mark near the hinge.
lots.condition: Light all-over wear and scratching, hinge and catch look intact, no dents seen.
lots.question_for_gowans: Please confirm the weight is 34.6g on your scale, and that the hinge and box clasp close and hold firmly.

lots.guide_summary: All sold, all Gowans hammer prices in AUD (rate 1.0); no unsold or asking evidence (no reachable retail source for emerald beads). Four loose '15-20 carats emerald gemstone beads' strands made $2 to $35 hammer (Jan to Aug 2026, median $25); these are loose, unclasped and uncertified, so close but not the same. Other finished gemstone bead necklaces at Gowans made $20 to $35 each.
lots.working: No same-item SOLD evidence: the only emerald bead sales at Gowans are loose strands without a clasp, and the lowest of them is a single-bid $2, so the formula gives $0 (2 / 1.198 = 1.7). No maximum bid. As a guide only, the loose strands made $25 to $35 hammer with 3 to 5 bids; a gold clasp, if confirmed, would add a few dollars of scrap value.
lots.confidence_reason: Emerald is unverified (no certificate, no test), the clasp shows no readable mark, and the only sales are close rather than same-item.
lots.dropped_entries: None dropped; all researcher prices, dates and titles matched the API. Generic gemstone necklaces, the tourmaline strand and the two-necklace lot kept only as category guides and left out of the guide range.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 2 enlarged: uneven, hand-cut rondelle facets with internal feathers and cloudy patches rather than round gas bubbles, which leans towards natural (probably oiled) emerald or possibly hydrothermal synthetic, though glass is not excluded. Colour is very saturated and even for small low-grade emerald, which is a caution. Clasp crop: gold-coloured barrel screw clasp with jump rings, no hallmark visible.
lots.condition: Beads look intact, no chips seen at this resolution; string and clasp appear sound.
lots.question_for_gowans: Is there any certificate or test for the beads, and is the clasp marked (9ct, 14k, 585) or plated? Total weight in carats or grams would also help.
